statement.essentials: A small neck muscle points to the nerve: the trunk lies just above its upper edge.
statement.anatomy: The trunk lies superior to the posterior belly of the digastric near its mastoid attachment; reported distances vary.

numbers.label: Posterior belly to trunk (cadaver)
numbers.population: 14 cadavers (22 live patients gave a mean of 10.7 mm, range 5 to 14)
numbers.design: Prospective measurement of the closest distance from the muscle's posterior-superior margin to the nerve

numbers.label: Posterior belly to trunk
numbers.design: Cadaveric measurement to the main trunk

numbers.label: Posterior belly to trunk
numbers.design: Micro-dissection, shortest distance from the muscle's attachment to the trunk

disagreement: Distances differ two- to three-fold between studies.
limitations: The studies measure from different points on the muscle and in different specimens; none is a measurement in a patient with a tumour. In the protocol the nerve is described as immediately above the muscle.
